changeability.rationale: Most high-traffic behavior (sprites, naming, formatting, moves-table sorting, home filtering) is centralized in one obvious place, but two real duplications — the species-card resolution block and per-list sort comparators — mean some fixes land 3–4 times.

app/components/MovesSection.tsx:31-38 — client component receives fully precomputed rows/tables from the server page; clean server/client seam

coupling.rationale: Loose coupling via narrow, typed props and a single data-layer facade; the one tangle is that lib/api.ts accumulates everything (URL construction, cache, records, media helpers) and two components inline type-badge markup instead of importing TypeBadge.

evidence: app/components/Section.tsx:1-19, app/components/PokemonCard.tsx, app/components/MovesSection.tsx — small, parameterized abstractions that stretch well across pages

app/app/moves/[name]/page.tsx:39-51 vs app/app/abilities/[name]/page.tsx:32-48 vs app/app/types/[name]/page.tsx:44-57 — three near-identical 'count + cards' page bodies with copy-pasted species resolution
app/components/TypeBadge.tsx:9-13 — link is a boolean flag, and three call sites bypass it entirely with inline type-badge Links (moves page:69, types page:82, MovesSection:173)

abstraction_design.rationale: The shared components are well-shaped, but the 'resource page with a Pokémon card list' pattern exists three times as copy-paste rather than as an abstraction, so an Items section means a fourth copy or an upfront refactor; minor boolean-flag creep on TypeBadge.

findings.issue: The Pokémon-refs → species-cards block (speciesById map, dedupe, alternate-form exclusion, dex sort) is duplicated in three page components; correctness-sensitive logic must be fixed three times.
findings.suggestion: Extract a helper in lib/api.ts, e.g. speciesCardsFor(refs: NamedResource[]): SpeciesIndexEntry[], and reuse it from the moves, abilities and types pages.

findings.issue: Type-badge Link markup is built inline here, in app/app/types/[name]/page.tsx:82 and in app/components/MovesSection.tsx:173, bypassing the existing TypeBadge component — a badge restyle or href change touches four places.
findings.suggestion: Use TypeBadge (with link) everywhere; if the non-link variant is needed on cards, keep the flag but route all badge rendering through it.

findings.issue: One 300-line module owns the API origin, fetch transport, in-memory cache, all record types, list munging and media-URL construction; a data-source change means editing this file plus the dynamic/revalidate/fetchCache exports repeated in 7 route segments.
findings.suggestion: Split into focused modules (transport+cache, records/types, media URLs) and drop the redundant `revalidate = 0` next to `force-dynamic`; consider a single source of truth for the no-store policy.

findings.issue: The home page builds the species→generation and species→types denormalizations inline; any change to how type/generation membership is derived lives in a page component rather than the data layer.
findings.suggestion: Move the index building into lib/api.ts (e.g. extend getAllSpecies/getAllTypes to return joined records) so pages only render.

findings.issue: getEnglishMoveName is exported but never imported anywhere — dead code that will confuse the next reader.
findings.suggestion: Delete it (the move pages call englishName directly).

findings.issue: The first() query-param helper is duplicated in app/app/page.tsx:28 — a param-parsing fix must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Move first() (and maybe a small parseQuery helper) into lib/format.ts or lib/api.ts.

findings.issue: EvolutionTree and EvolutionBranch are near-identical recursive components; a change to the nested-list rendering must be made in both.
findings.suggestion: Collapse to one recursive component (EvolutionTree can just delegate to it) or extract a shared SpeciesLink.

findings.issue: One flat global stylesheet of 620 lines with feature-specific selectors (.hidden-label for ability cards, .moves-table, .damage-relations, ...); removing a feature leaves dead CSS that only a manual audit finds.
findings.suggestion: Co-locate route-specific CSS (Next.js supports per-segment CSS imports or CSS Modules) or at least group/comment selectors by route so deletions are greppable.

findings.issue: The ~290-line page component mixes fetch orchestration with heavy row/method munging inline, making targeted edits to the Moves section require understanding the whole page.
findings.suggestion: Extract the game/rows/tables derivation into a pure function (e.g. buildMovesTables(pokemon, selectedGame)) that is trivially testable and keeps the page to rendering.

summary: A small, consistently layered codebase: typed data facade, narrow prop-driven components, and a clean server/client split make most fixes land in one obvious place (frontSpriteUrl, format.ts, MovesSection). The recurring weakness is copy-paste at the page level — the species-card resolution block, sort comparators, and type-badge markup are each duplicated 3–4 times — so extensions like an Items section risk a fourth copy, and feature removal leaves dead code in api.ts and globals.css. Well above the bar for a PR, with a clear list of low-risk consolidations.
